findings.description: When the last attempt fails, the code logs and breaks out of the loop, and the function falls off the end and returns None. settle_invoice only catches GatewayError, so it treats the None as a successful charge and executes `charge.id`, raising AttributeError. That AttributeError escapes settle_open_invoices and aborts the whole batch. The invoice is never marked PAYMENT_FAILED and the remaining invoices are not processed.
findings.suggestion: Keep the last exception and re-raise it after the loop, e.g. `raise` inside the `if attempt == attempts:` branch instead of `break`.
findings.title: charge() returns None after retries are exhausted instead of raising GatewayError

findings.description: settle_invoice calls charge(..., idempotency_key=...) which works with the wrapper's parameter name. However, the wrapper forwards the key positionally to the underlying gateway, which may name or order its parameters differently, so it can pass it to the wrong parameter.
findings.suggestion: Forward the key by keyword: self._gateway.charge(customer_id, amount_cents, currency, idempotency_key=idempotency_key).
findings.title: Gateway is invoked with an idempotency_key keyword that RetryingGateway's positional signature must match
